newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives press Labour on windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives press Labour on windfall tax.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservatives on Monday stepped up a war of words over over the opposition Labour party's proposed windfall tax on privatised utlities by claiming the levy would cost British customers indirectly an average of about 192 pounds.

Conservative party chairman Brian Mawhinney told a news conference the bill was "heartstopping". He said: "The windfall tax is Labour's new tax on bills, jobs and pensions. It's a tax on the utilities, it's a tax on you."

In an attempt to smoke out Labour ahead of a parliamentary debate on Thursday on the planned levy, Mawhinney challenged its economics spokesman, Gordon Brown, to publish his own calculations if he disagreed with the Conservatives' estimate.

"Tell us how much they calculate the windfall tax would put on bills. Tell us how many jobs they think it would cost. Tell us what they think it would do to shares in the companies and therefore pensions which depend on those shares.
"In short, publish or be damned," Mawhinney said.
The figure of 192 pounds is based on a projection by investment bank Goldman Sachs that Labour would aim to raise five billion pounds from taxing the excess profits of privatised utilities.
The total liability for each utility was then divided by its total number of customers to give the cost per customer.
